tests.description: Reference: WRF 4.8 em_scm_xy single-column run (GNU gfortran 13.3 REAL*4 build, dt = 60 s, damp_opt = 2 dampcoef = 0.003 zdamp = 5000 m, pert_coriolis = .true., use_theta_m = 1, hybrid_opt = 0; data/eqwefic/scm_dyn, the scm_ref namelist re-run with the instrumented binary) dumped by the ctessum-claude/WRF fork, branch earthsciml-instrumented, commit 83347b2 (dyn_em/module_em.F rk_tendency, rk_step 1 of the step; module_esm_dump), merged with the same step's radiation subassembly dump and the wrfout eta grid by tools/merge_dumps.py into data/eqwefic/dumps/dyn_column/esm_dump_dyn_suite_<step>.json. The rebuilt binary reproduces the archived scm_ref radiation subassembly dumps bit for bit (all but the three B9 variables). The column is horizontally uniform (u, v identical in the two tile columns, ww = 0, all map factors 1, c1 = 1, c2 = 0). Expected tendencies are the dumped mass-coupled increments of the named routine divided by the coupling mass of their grid point (muu, muv, mut), i.e. the instantaneous decoupled rate at the time-level-n state; references are single precision, so tolerances follow the rel 1e-5 real32 convention, with absolute Linf bounds on whole profiles where values pass through zero. Routine: pg_buoy_w (dyn_em/module_big_step_utilities_em.F), with the moisture coefficient of calc_cq; the eta grid is the run's wrfout ZNW (single precision), the total water the sum of the six WSM6 species from the same step's radiation subassembly dump. The w tendency is a near-cancellation of O(g mu_b q) terms (~2e3 Pa m/s^2 against a residual of ~10), so single-precision rounding in the Fortran sum sets the floor: measured residual Linf <= 6.0e-9 m/s^2 over the three regimes against values <= 5.9e-4 (1e-5 of the profile maximum), well above the esm evaluation's own rounding. dphi_dt = g w is the geopotential equation of advance_w (dyn_em/module_small_step_em.F) and has no separate Fortran tendency to assert. Regime: step 60 (t = 1 h, early afternoon, convective boundary layer).

input_q_t.expr: rad_qv + rad_qc + rad_qr + rad_qi + rad_qs + rad_qg
